summary.headline: JTL Industries Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR722 crore with EBITDA INR59 crore (8.1% margin) and volumes up 17.8% YoY to 118,513 MT.
summary.overview: JTL Industries reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA in Q1 FY27, with revenue of INR722 crore, EBITDA of INR59 crore and PAT of INR35 crore (4.9% margin). PAT absorbed INR2.8 crore of extra non-cash depreciation from the March 2026 revaluation at JTL Defence. Operational EBITDA per ton excluding other income was INR4,954, which management attributed to product mix and efficiency; it said JTL Defence added about INR200 per ton to consolidated figures. Management reiterated FY27 volume growth of at least 30%, with Mangaon capacity expansion of about 1 million tons targeted by end H1 and capex of about INR100 crore left to reach 2 million tons.

financial_highlights.change: Margin 4.9%; after INR2.8 crore extra depreciation from JTL Defence revaluation

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA per ton (ex other income)

segments.name: JTL Industries (steel tubes and pipes)
segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton about INR4,750 excluding JTL Defence; DFT structural pipes now running at 20,000-25,000 tons per quarter, roughly double the prior ~10,000 tons. Mangaon facility utilisation about 42%.

segments.name: JTL Defence (ex-RCI Industries & Technologies)
segments.commentary: Run rate about 100 MT/month in Q1, with about 120 MT in the first month of Q2. Q1 EBITDA margin about 12%, versus about 20% in Q4 which included inventory gains. Management targets 500 MT/month by Q4 FY27 and INR150 crore top line this year.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA per ton: JTL Steel tube and pipe segment ~INR4,750 seen as sustainable; management confident of reaching INR5,000 consolidated in coming quarters; FY27 target had been ~INR4,500.
FY27 volume growth of at least 30% reiterated; H2 expected stronger than H1, and management aims to exceed 30%.
Company utilisation ~55% now, targeted ~65% by year-end FY27; Mangaon utilisation to rise toward ~60%.

Capacity: ~7 lakh tons to be commissioned by end H1 FY27; remaining 3 lakh tons (API pipes) by about the same time next year. Full utilisation by FY29; utilisation 50-60% in FY29; peak ~70% possibly FY29-FY30.
Peak revenue potential on the current capex cycle: ~1.4 million tons at ~INR65,000/ton, about INR9,100 crore (management's arithmetic).
Value-added share target of 50-60% of products once the 2 million ton capacity is complete.
Export target of 10% of total sales for coming quarters; export order book of about INR75 crore.
Capex: ~INR100 crore in FY27 to complete the expansion, then maintenance capex of INR30-40 crore a year; JTL Defence capex about INR15 crore this year and similar next year.
FY28 working capital cycle target of 35-40 days.
JTL Defence EBITDA margin long-term 15%; 10-15% band expected over time, with near-term wavering likely.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 1 million tons; expansion to 2 million tons planned, with about 7 lakh tons commissioning by end H1 FY27.
Mangaon facility utilisation about 42%; producing about 7,000-10,000 tons of DFT a quarter there, with room to double.
Remaining INR100 crore of capex in FY27 completes the expansion; maintenance capex INR30-40 crore a year after that.
JTL Defence: capacity about 1,000 tons/month on the hot plant; INR15 crore capex in FY27 for coin and bullet shell lines, which changes product mix rather than capacity.
demand_pricing: Secondary demand described as record-breaking; primary-secondary spread ranged INR8-12/kg in Q1 (versus a normal INR4-5/kg), and management says it remains at that level.
Company has about 45-50% capacity allocated to the secondary market; dealer network contributes 50-60% of sales, with 7-8 day dealer payment cycles.
Government share of sales fell to under 5% last year from over 25% earlier; company deliberately shifting to dealers and exports, with DFT sold direct to bodies such as MMRDA and airport authorities.
Exports affected by Hormuz-related container and logistics shortages; company received ACRS certification (mainly Australia) and has started shipments to the US, Mexico and Canada.
July 2026 described as an all-time high month; management expects another record quarter.
Gaining share in DFT, specialised high-diameter/high-thickness products, and seamless-pipe replacement for hydraulic and automotive OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR5,000 per ton EBITDA a one-off or structural, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JTL Defence added about INR200/ton; ex-Defence EBITDA was about INR4,750/ton, and INR5,000 consolidated is expected in coming quarters on the back of product mix and normalised HRC.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% volume growth guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said H2 will be stronger and it expects to exceed 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity ramp and utilisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: 7 lakh tons by end H1; the remaining 3 lakh tons (API pipes) by about the same time next year. Utilisation 50-60% in FY29; peak about 70%, possibly FY29 or FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential at peak utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.4 million tons at INR65,000-66,000/ton, roughly INR9,100 crore on the current capex cycle.

qa_highlights.question: JTL Defence guidance and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Run rate about 100 MT/month in Q1, about 120 MT in the first month of Q2; target 500 MT/month by Q4 FY27. Long-term margin 15%, with 10-15% expected over time.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Cycle down to about 75 days from 90; target 35-40 days by FY28, helped by dealer financing and a shift away from government receivables.

risks_watch: Export lag: exports fell to 5% of sales in Q1 on Hormuz-related container and logistics shortages; management targets 10% of sales and says the delayed INR75 crore export order book will be shipped in coming quarters if logistics improve.

Secondary-market dependence: management says demand and margins rely on the primary-secondary spread staying at INR8-12/kg versus a normal INR4-5/kg; a narrowing spread would reduce the secondary demand tailwind.

Capacity ramp timing: 7 lakh tons due by end H1 FY27, with the remaining 3 lakh tons of API pipes about a year later; management said FY29 utilisation depends on when that last leg is completed, and the 70% peak could come in FY29 or FY30.

JTL Defence margin volatility: Q1 EBITDA margin about 12% versus about 20% in Q4 (inflated by inventory gains); management says 15% is the long-term margin, with 10-15% wavering near term, and the 500 MT/month exit target by Q4 FY27 requires a rise from about 120 MT in the first month of Q2.
Consolidated EBITDA per ton: management guided ~INR4,500 for FY27 earlier but now targets INR5,000 consolidated in coming quarters; the ex-Defence ~INR4,750 figure depends on normalised HRC prices.
Working capital: cycle at ~75 days versus a FY28 target of 35-40 days; management attributes the improvement to dealer financing and reduced government receivables.
key_quotes: So, we are very confident that consolidated level, INR5,000 is something that we'll definitely see in the coming quarters as well.
It's too soon again to maintain the exact 15% margin going ahead, but the long -term margin is 15%.
So, it's safe to say that 30% will be automobile and dealer network, 35% will be defense and the remaining will be mint factories.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on demand, volume guidance, EBITDA per ton and the capacity build-out, repeatedly reiterating targets. It was more cautious and hedged on JTL Defence margins (described as new and still being tested), exact utilisation timing for the final 3 lakh tons, and export shipments disrupted by logistics.
